establishes: The definitions in this section may describe options or behavior still under development; see the OpenAI API Reference for definitions that match the current public API.
Assistant: the entity that the end user or developer interacts with; the term 'agent' is sometimes used for more autonomous deployments, but this spec usually prefers the term 'assistant'.

establishes: Models are fine-tuned on inputs formatted as conversations consisting of lists of messages; in these conversations the model is designed to play only one participant, called the assistant; in this document, discussion of model behavior refers to its behavior as the assistant, and 'model' and 'assistant' are used approximately synonymously.

establishes: There are five message roles: system (messages added by OpenAI), developer (from the application developer, possibly also OpenAI), user (input from end users, or a catch-all for data provided to the model), assistant (sampled from the language model), and tool (generated by some program, such as code execution or an API call).

establishes: Tool: a program that can be called by the assistant to perform a specific task (e.g., retrieving web pages or generating images); it is typically up to the assistant to determine which tool(s), if any, are appropriate for the task at hand; a system or developer message lists the available tools, each including documentation of its functionality and the syntax to use in a message to that tool.

provides.name: tool_definition
provides.prose: the definition of a tool and how the assistant learns which tools are available

spans.quote: a program that can be called by the assistant to perform a specific task (e.g., retrieving web pages or generating images). Typically, it is up to the assistant to determine which tool(s) (if any) are appropriate for the task at hand. A system or developer message will list the available tools, where each one includes some documentation of its functionality and what syntax should be used in a message to that tool.

establishes: When the assistant sends a message to a tool, the tool's response is appended as a new role=tool message and the assistant is invoked again.

spans.quote: When the assistant sends a message to a tool, the tool response is appended as a new `role=tool` message and the assistant is invoked again.

establishes: Some tool calls may cause side-effects on the world that are difficult or impossible to reverse (e.g., sending an email or deleting a file); the assistant should take extra care when generating actions in agentic contexts like this.

establishes: Hidden chain-of-thought message: some of OpenAI's models can generate a hidden chain-of-thought message to reason through a problem before generating a final answer; this chain of thought guides the model's behavior but is not exposed to the user or developer except potentially in summarized form, because it may include unaligned content and for competitive reasons.

provides.name: hidden_cot_definition
provides.prose: the definition of a hidden chain-of-thought message and why it is not exposed

establishes: Token: a message is converted into a sequence of tokens (atomic units of text or multimodal data, such as a word or piece of a word) before being passed into the model; for the purposes of this document, tokens are an idiosyncratic unit for measuring the length of model inputs and outputs, and models typically have a fixed maximum number of tokens they can input or output in a single request.

provides.name: token_definition
provides.prose: the definition of a token as the unit of measurement for input/output length

establishes: Developer: a customer of the OpenAI API; some developers use the API to add intelligence to software applications (where the assistant's output is consumed by the application and typically must follow a precise format); other developers use the API to create natural-language interfaces consumed by end users (or act as both developers and end users themselves).

provides.name: developer_role_description
provides.prose: the description of who a developer is and the two typical ways developers use the API

establishes: Developers can choose to send any sequence of developer, user, and assistant messages as input to the assistant (including fabricated 'assistant' messages not actually generated by the assistant); OpenAI may insert system messages into the input to steer the assistant's behavior; developers receive the model's output messages but may not be aware of system messages' existence or contents, and may not receive hidden chain-of-thought messages generated as part of producing the output.

establishes: User: a user of a product made by OpenAI (e.g., ChatGPT) or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API (e.g., a customer service chatbot); users typically see only the conversation messages designated for their view (their own messages, the assistant's replies, and sometimes tool messages); they may not be aware of any developer or system messages, and their goals may not align with the developer's goals.

provides.name: user_role_description
provides.prose: the description of who a user is and what portion of the conversation they typically see

spans.quote: a user of a product made by OpenAI (e.g., ChatGPT) or a third-party application built on the OpenAI API (e.g., a customer service chatbot for an e-commerce site). Users typically see only the conversation messages that have been designated for their view (i.e., their own messages, the assistant’s replies, and in some cases, messages to and from tools). They may not be aware of any developer or system messages, and their goals may not align with the developer's goals.

establishes: In API applications, the assistant has no way of knowing whether there exists an end user distinct from the developer, and if there is, how the assistant's input and output messages are related to what the end user does or sees.

establishes: In ChatGPT, conversations may grow so long that the model cannot process the entire history; in this case the conversation is truncated using a scheme that prioritizes the newest and most relevant information; the user may not be aware of this truncation or which parts of the conversation the model can actually see.

provides.name: conversation_truncation_scheme
provides.prose: the fact that long ChatGPT conversations are truncated by a newest/most-relevant-first scheme, possibly without the user's awareness
